compiled_state.title: Add concurrent-write fixture proving fcntl.flock prevents lost writes in append_review_cycle.py
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story DD Coverage
- dd-4: Concurrent-write fixture passes: two concurrent writers each appending one cycle entry result in cycles[] containing both entries (no lost writes)

## Testing Mode
RED (creates fixture that exercises locking guarantee)

## Files to Modify
- tests/scripts/test-append-review-cycle-concurrent.sh (Create)
- plugins/dso/scripts/append_review_cycle.py (Edit — only if lock-acquisition hardening required)

## Given/When/Then
Given tmpdir review artifact initialized with {cycles:[]}; When two append_review_cycle.py processes launched in parallel with --n 1 and --n 2; Then cycles[] has length 2 with both n=1 and n=2 (no lost writes).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. tests/scripts/test-append-review-cycle-concurrent.sh exists and is executable
2. Concurrent fixture passes on at least 3 consecutive runs (no flake)
3. Both n=1 and n=2 entries present in cycles[] after concurrent run
4. Both processes exit with code 0
5. Run: bash tests/scripts/test-append-review-cycle-concurrent.sh → PASS
6. Run: ruff check plugins/dso/scripts/append_review_cycle.py → PASS (if edited)

comments.body:
GAP_ANALYSIS_AC_AMENDMENT: Concurrent fixture must use OS processes (not threads)

Amend AC to add:
- Fixture spawns N>=3 independent OS processes (not threads, not asyncio) — fcntl.flock is per-process, thread-based test would falsely pass
- Assert final cycles[] length == N, all n values present exactly once (no overwrites)
- Assert file is valid JSON at every intermediate step (no torn writes → verifies atomic rename pattern)
- Recommend: use subprocess.Popen or shell '&' + 'wait' to spawn multiple processes
